text: Adopted the neoclassical utility-maximisation framework for the consumer-theory track; preferences are encoded as a complete transitive ordering representable by a continuous utility function under mild regularity.

utility maximisation consumer preference complete transitive continuous function

text: Hal Varian's Intermediate Microeconomics is the primary textbook for the undergraduate sequence; the ninth-edition chapter on Slutsky decomposition drives the problem sets in week six.

queries.text: which undergraduate textbook anchors the sequence and whose chapter feeds the Slutsky problem sets
varian intermediate microeconomics textbook slutsky undergraduate reference

text: Mas-Colell, Whinston and Green's Microeconomic Theory is the graduate reference; chapters one through three formalise preferences, choice, and demand before any production theory enters the story.

queries.text: which graduate text formalises preferences and choice before production and who authored it
mas colell whinston green microeconomic theory graduate preference choice demand

text: An indifference curve is the level set of a utility function in commodity space; strict convexity of preferences gives curves that bow toward the origin and a unique interior optimum.

queries.text: what geometric object represents equal-utility bundles and which property of preferences gives a unique optimum
indifference curve level set utility convex preference interior optimum

text: Marshallian demand solves the consumer's problem at fixed income; the Lagrangian on the budget constraint yields demand as a function of prices and wealth with the tangency condition setting the MRS equal to the price ratio.

queries.text: how does the fixed-income consumer problem derive demand and what tangency condition characterises the optimum
marshallian demand lagrangian budget mrs price ratio tangency wealth

text: Hicksian demand solves the dual expenditure-minimisation problem at a fixed utility target; it isolates the pure substitution response and never slopes upward in its own price.

queries.text: how does the compensated demand problem isolate substitution effects and what sign restriction does it enforce
hicksian demand expenditure minimisation substitution compensated dual

text: The Slutsky equation decomposes a Marshallian demand price effect into a Hicksian demand substitution term and an income term weighted by the initial quantity; the lecture uses it to sign cross-price effects for normal goods.

queries.text: which identity splits a price effect into substitution and income pieces and what does it sign for normal goods
slutsky equation decomposition marshallian hicksian substitution income price effect

text: Paul Samuelson introduced the Weak Axiom of Revealed Preference in 1938, recasting demand theory without appealing to unobservable utility and opening the door to the integrability problem.

queries.text: which 1938 axiom recast demand theory without utility and what open question did it raise
samuelson 1938 weak axiom revealed preference utility integrability demand

text: Revealed-preference theory infers ordinal preferences from observed choices; the Strong Axiom of Revealed Preference strengthens the Weak Axiom of Revealed Preference by ruling out cycles of any length in the revealed-at-least-as-good relation.

queries.text: which choice-based theory recovers preferences from data and how does the strong version strengthen the weak one
revealed preference strong weak axiom cycle observed choice ordinal

The firm's production function maps input bundles into a maximum output; isoquants are its level sets and the marginal rate of technical substitution plays the role of the MRS on the cost side.

queries.text: how does producer theory mirror consumer theory and what object plays the role of the MRS on the production side
production function isoquant mrts input output level set firm

text: Chose the Cobb-Douglas production function as the baseline for the firm-theory problem set; its constant output elasticities and unit elasticity of substitution make the cost-minimisation algebra clean.

queries.text: which production function serves as the baseline for the problem set and which algebraic properties recommended it
cobb douglas production elasticity substitution cost minimisation firm baseline

text: The CES production function nests Cobb-Douglas, Leontief, and linear technologies as limits of its substitution parameter; the elasticity of substitution is constant along every isoquant by construction.

queries.text: which functional form nests Cobb-Douglas and Leontief as limits and what stays constant along its isoquants
ces production function cobb douglas leontief linear elasticity substitution

text: The returns to scale property describes how output changes when every input scales by a common factor; a homogeneous production function of degree k above one exhibits increasing returns and gives decreasing long-run average cost.

queries.text: what property of the production function controls returns to scale and how does it shape long-run average cost
returns scale homogeneous production degree increasing decreasing long run average

text: The cost function is derived by solving the firm's cost-minimisation problem given factor prices; Shephard's lemma recovers conditional factor demand as the partial derivative of cost with respect to the input price.

queries.text: how is the cost function obtained from the firm problem and which lemma recovers conditional factor demands
cost function minimisation shephard lemma conditional factor demand input price

text: The perfect competition model is adopted as the benchmark market structure: price-taking firms, free entry and exit, homogeneous product, and perfect information jointly pin down the long-run zero-profit condition.

queries.text: which market-structure benchmark combines four assumptions to force long-run zero profits
perfect competition price taking free entry homogeneous zero profit long run

text: A monopoly faces the whole downward-sloping market demand and sets marginal revenue equal to marginal cost; the resulting Lerner index measures the markup as a function of the own-price elasticity of demand.

queries.text: which optimality condition characterises a monopoly price and which index reads off the resulting markup
monopoly marginal revenue cost lerner index markup elasticity demand

text: The monopolistic competition framework is used to model differentiated-product retail; the Dixit-Stiglitz symmetric equilibrium pins down firm-level markups via the elasticity of substitution across varieties.

queries.text: which oligopoly framework models differentiated retail and what pins down firm-level markups in its symmetric equilibrium
monopolistic competition dixit stiglitz differentiated variety elasticity markup

text: Cournot duopoly fixes quantities as strategic variables and solves for a Nash equilibrium in best-response quantities; equilibrium output lies strictly between the monopoly and competitive levels.

queries.text: which oligopoly model treats quantity as the strategic variable and where does its equilibrium output sit
cournot duopoly quantity nash best response monopoly competitive output

text: Bertrand competition makes price the strategic variable with homogeneous goods; any price above marginal cost is undercut, so the unique equilibrium collapses to marginal-cost pricing and the Bertrand paradox.

queries.text: which oligopoly model pushes price to marginal cost with homogeneous goods and what puzzle does it produce
bertrand competition price marginal cost undercut paradox homogeneous equilibrium

text: Stackelberg leadership resolves the Cournot duopoly by giving one firm the move first; the leader internalises the follower's best-response function and secures a first-mover output advantage.

queries.text: which oligopoly variant sequences moves and what informational advantage does the leader exploit
stackelberg leader follower cournot sequential best response first mover

text: Antoine Augustin Cournot introduced the quantity-setting duopoly model in 1838 in Recherches sur les principes mathematiques de la theorie des richesses, anticipating Nash equilibrium by more than a century.

entities.name: Recherches sur les principes mathematiques de la theorie des richesses

relationships.source: Recherches sur les principes mathematiques de la theorie des richesses

queries.text: which 1838 monograph introduced quantity-setting duopoly and which later solution concept did it anticipate
cournot 1838 recherches richesses duopoly quantity nash equilibrium precursor

text: Joseph Bertrand published his 1883 review of Cournot duopoly in the Journal des Savants and pointed out that price competition collapses the duopoly markup; the critique seeded a century of oligopoly debate.

queries.text: which 1883 review argued price competition collapses the duopoly markup and where did it appear
bertrand 1883 journal savants cournot review price competition markup critique

text: The study of externalities is adopted as the canonical market-failure case; a negative externality drives a wedge between the private and social marginal cost curves and yields a deadweight loss at the unregulated equilibrium.

queries.text: which class of market failure drives a wedge between private and social cost and what efficiency loss follows
externality market failure social private marginal cost deadweight loss wedge

text: Ronald Coase's 1960 paper The Problem of Social Cost published in the Journal of Law and Economics argued that with clearly assigned property rights and zero transaction costs, bargaining internalises externalities regardless of who holds the right.

queries.text: which 1960 paper argued that property rights and zero transaction costs let bargaining cure externalities
coase 1960 problem social cost journal law economics property rights bargaining

text: A Pigouvian tax sets the per-unit tax equal to the marginal external damage at the social optimum; the unregulated market then internalises the wedge without requiring quantity regulation.

queries.text: which per-unit tax aligns private and social marginal cost and how is its rate chosen
pigouvian tax marginal external damage social optimum internalise wedge

text: The Coase theorem is preferred over Pigouvian taxation when transaction costs are low and property rights can be clearly assigned; the Pigouvian lever wins when bargaining fails due to numerous parties or hidden damages.

queries.text: when is bargaining preferred to a Pigouvian tax for correcting an externality and what flips the preference
coase theorem pigouvian tax transaction cost property right bargaining prefer

text: A public good is non-rival and non-excludable by assumption; the Samuelson condition characterises efficient provision by equating the sum of marginal rates of substitution across consumers to the marginal rate of transformation.

queries.text: which two properties define a public good and which condition pins down the efficient level of provision
public good non rival non excludable samuelson condition mrs mrt efficient

text: The free-rider problem blocks voluntary provision of public goods: each consumer prefers to understate willingness to pay, so decentralised contributions fall short of the level prescribed by the Samuelson condition.

queries.text: which incentive failure undermines voluntary public-good provision and what benchmark does it miss
free rider public good samuelson willingness to pay voluntary provision

text: Lindahl pricing restores efficiency in public goods by charging each consumer a personalised price equal to her marginal valuation; the common quantity at which budgets balance delivers a Pareto-efficient allocation.

queries.text: which personalised-price scheme delivers efficient public-good provision and what balances at the common quantity
lindahl pricing public good personalised marginal valuation pareto efficient

text: George Akerlof's 1970 paper The Market for Lemons published in the Quarterly Journal of Economics showed that asymmetric information can collapse a used-car market into low-quality trade only, founding modern information economics.

queries.text: which 1970 paper showed asymmetric information can unravel a used-car market and where did it appear
akerlof 1970 lemons quarterly journal asymmetric information economics

text: The adverse selection failure hits insurance markets when asymmetric information stops insurers distinguishing high-risk from low-risk applicants at the posted premium; low-risk types exit and the pool deteriorates into the high-risk corner.

queries.text: which asymmetric-information failure empties insurance pools of low-risk buyers and what is the end state
adverse selection insurance premium asymmetric information risk pool unravel

text: The moral hazard problem arises after a contract is signed when the insured action is unobservable to the principal; the risk-sharing contract must trade full insurance against incentives to exert costly effort.

queries.text: which post-contract information failure forces a trade-off between insurance and incentives
moral hazard unobservable effort principal agent insurance incentive risk

text: The principal-agent problem sets up a risk-neutral principal writing a contract for a risk-averse agent whose effort is a hidden action; the optimal contract ties pay to a noisy performance signal balancing insurance and effort incentives.

queries.text: how does the principal-agent model structure contracts when effort is hidden and what does optimal pay depend on
principal agent risk averse hidden effort performance signal contract insurance

text: Michael Spence's 1973 paper Job Market Signaling published in the Quarterly Journal of Economics introduced signaling theory and showed that costly education can separate high- from low-productivity workers in equilibrium even when education adds no productivity.

queries.text: which 1973 paper used education as a separating device without any productivity effect
spence 1973 job market signaling quarterly journal education productivity separate

text: A separating equilibrium in the Spence signaling model requires the single-crossing condition: high-type indifference curves in effort-wage space must cross low-type curves from below at every point.

queries.text: which geometric condition on indifference curves supports a separating equilibrium in the signaling model
separating equilibrium spence signaling single crossing condition indifference

text: Rothschild and Stiglitz's 1976 paper Equilibrium in Competitive Insurance Markets published in the Quarterly Journal of Economics introduced screening via self-selecting menus and showed pooling equilibria need not exist in competitive insurance.

queries.text: which 1976 paper introduced screening in insurance and what equilibrium existence result did it prove
rothschild stiglitz 1976 equilibrium competitive insurance screening pooling

text: Used Spence signaling to model sheepskin effects on wages and Rothschild-Stiglitz screening to model insurance menus; signaling moves first with the informed party, screening moves first with the uninformed.

queries.text: which information-economics tool fits wage premia from credentials and which fits insurance menu design
signaling screening spence rothschild stiglitz informed uninformed move order

text: The general equilibrium theory framework closes the consumer and firm problems into a single system: prices clear all markets simultaneously and Walras's law makes one market-clearing condition redundant once the others hold.

queries.text: how does general-equilibrium theory close consumer and firm problems and why is one market-clearing condition redundant
general equilibrium walras law market clearing simultaneous prices consumer firm

text: The Arrow-Debreu model is the canonical general-equilibrium reference for the graduate sequence; Gerard Debreu's 1959 Theory of Value monograph axiomatised the framework that the 1954 existence paper established.

queries.text: which Arrow-Debreu monograph axiomatises general equilibrium and who wrote it
arrow debreu theory value 1959 debreu general equilibrium axiomatisation

text: The First Welfare Theorem states that every competitive equilibrium is Pareto efficient under local non-satiation; the proof is elementary and does not require convexity of preferences.

queries.text: which welfare theorem links competitive equilibrium to Pareto efficiency and what minimal assumption drives the proof
first welfare theorem competitive equilibrium pareto efficient local non satiation

text: The Second Welfare Theorem says any Pareto-efficient allocation can be decentralised as a competitive equilibrium after appropriate lump-sum transfers, provided convex preferences and convex production sets hold.

queries.text: which welfare theorem decentralises an efficient allocation via transfers and what convexity assumption does it need
second welfare theorem pareto lump sum transfer convex preference decentralise

mankiw principles economics introductory undergraduate prose first varian consumer
